editorial:
Imagine your dad is the most boring guy in the neighborhood, selling cars and grilling burgers, but he used to be a deadly assassin. That is the wild setup of this action comedy, and it works better than you might expect. Mark Wahlberg plays Dan Morgan, a family man whose quiet life gets blown up when old enemies track him down. Instead of telling his wife and kids the truth, he packs everyone into the minivan for a surprise road trip to Las Vegas. The kids think it is a fun vacation. The wife thinks it is a romantic getaway. Dan knows it is a fight for survival. The movie leans hard into the contrast between suburban dad life and spy movie chaos, and that contrast is where most of the laughs come from.

The action scenes are surprisingly well done, with car chases and fight sequences that feel big without being too serious. Wahlberg is comfortable in this kind of role, and Michelle Monaghan brings warmth as his wife. The kids add heart and humor. On the downside, the plot is pretty predictable, and some jokes land flat. Still, if you want a fun movie night with popcorn, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final act, Dan's family learns the truth about his past during a showdown in Las Vegas. His old boss and former partner come after him, but Dan uses his assassin skills to protect his family. The big twist is that his wife Jessica already knew about his past and had been keeping secrets of her own. She helps him fight back, and together they take down the bad guys. The family survives, and Dan finally comes clean. They return home as a stronger, more honest family, with Dan leaving his dangerous past behind for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action comedies with heart and family road trip chaos.
